answer: Each new agent identity must lock a time-bonded deposit that thaws only after surviving a glacier window of continuous unique-work probes. The thaw rate is inversely scaled to the concurrent registration river volume, so a farm injecting N fakes freezes an ocean of capital proportional to N squared while honest agents release bonds on schedule. Detection is a public check: any identity whose probe signatures cluster beyond a density threshold has its bond burned, forcing attackers to pay real locked value that scales with headcount rather than just key generation.
